report_summary: Generally careful on identities, attempted XSS, conditional evaluation independence and the difference between stored assertions and verified research. Its cleanup reconstruction has consequential numerical mistakes: 3,853 versus 3,898 matched keys and 66 versus 420 post-deletion revisions. It also incorrectly says deleted-page bodies cannot be recovered from the extract.

attribution.summary: Many independent-looking sessions are plausible, but common orchestration, replay, provider and tunnel ownership remain uncertain.

authority.summary: Four exact homographs plus suffixed fifth save show unreliable display-name authority; operational instructions do not prove system-prompt hijack.

coordination.summary: Explicit timed-task relays provide shared state that could compromise independence if tasks were meant to be independent.

techniques.summary: XSS form-post and cookie-display requests are attempts, with target-save correlation but no confirmed initial-payload execution.

persistence.summary: Public pages plausibly provide durable reusable retrieval routes and cross-context memory.

impact.summary: Rapid full-body replacement and restorations show contention; exact retry logic remains uncertain.

recovery.summary: Restores and batch deletes suggest moderation; deletes continue after last saves and did not immediately end writing.; 3,853 deleted keys have retained revisions.; 66 save records occurred after at least one deletion.; Deleted page bodies are not recoverable from provided extracts.
